text: Physical mechanical impedance induces extracellular ATP release and triggers purinoceptor-mediated inhibition of primary root elongation in Arabidopsis thaliana.
Exogenous apyrase hydrolyzes apoplastic eATP, relieving purinoceptor activation and rescuing primary root elongation under mechanical impedance.

The root growth trial is structured as a Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with N = 72 seedlings across 4 blocks and 3 treatments (Control, Impedance, Impedance_Apyrase), with 24 seedlings per treatment and 6 seedlings per block-treatment cell.

Linear mixed-effects modeling with random block intercepts reveals substantial environmental clustering across blocks (ICC = 0.536, sigma2_block = 1.631, sigma2_residual = 1.412), reducing error variance by 47.5% relative to unblocked OLS.

Treatment exerts a highly significant effect on primary root length (F(2, 66) = 491.16, p < 0.0001, Kenward-Roger df), with model estimated marginal means of 22.56 mm (Control), 11.93 mm (Impedance), and 18.63 mm (Impedance_Apyrase) (SE = 0.68 mm).

Mechanical impedance decreases root length by 10.63 mm (t(66) = 30.99, p < 0.0001), while exogenous apyrase supplementation restores 6.70 mm (t(66) = -19.54, p < 0.0001, Tukey-adjusted), yielding a 63.0% recovery of the impedance growth penalty.
The trial data are classified as SIMULATED_BENCHMARK_DATA generated for certification benchmarking rather than live physiological measurements.
